11.description: The Committee on Environment and Utilities will no longer distribute city materials, focusing instead on its own mandate and work. It will use custom flyers and QR codes to direct residents to city information.

chips.text: Committee members expressed concern over a 'lost opportunity' to share city information.
Staff clarified the committee's mandate does not include promoting specific city programs.
Clarity is still needed on specific materials the committee can distribute.
The new policy limits the committee's ability to promote city environmental programs.
Staff will provide more clarity on material distribution at the next meeting.

19.description: The Sump Pump Discharge Review Project is exploring options to address high groundwater levels causing sump pumps to constantly discharge, leading to saturated green spaces and icy sidewalks for residents.

chips.text: No silver bullet found yet for sump pump discharge issues.
Project focuses on future development, not existing sump pump issues.
Residents have informed council and expressed frustration on social media.
Sharing developer data could lead to legal issues and devalue lots.
Discharging clean water to sanitary system is not ideal for treatment.
Staff will engage industry this summer on potential solutions.

15.description: The Water Conservation and Quality Management Subcommittee will focus on development guidelines, water conservation education, microplastics, and water system upgrades.

chips.text: Whether an extra pipe for experimental treatment systems was installed is unknown.
Water-related initiatives linked to biosolids project and system upgrades.
